thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P1 — SRV lookup failures detected in us-east-1b (service-discovery). Pager triggered: oncall@infra. Link: https://redwood.internal/incident/1977778888

alex: oncall here, got paged 02:12 UTC. Seeing spikes in SRV lookup errors from runtime on a subset of AZs (us-east-1b). Internal control-plane -> service talk failing intermittently.

samir: confirming. Metrics: consul/etcd SRV query error rate up ~42% in us-east-1b over last 6m. CoreDNS pods in that AZ showing increased SERVFAILs.

alex: example from app logs: 
```
2026-03-15T02:10:43Z app[router]: lookup service.svc.cluster.local: SRV query returned SERVFAIL (retry)
2026-03-15T02:10:44Z app[router]: fallback to health-checking, 504 to upstream
```

june_ops: running quick dig from a node in us-east-1b: 
```
$ dig +short SRV _api._tcp.service.namespace.svc.cluster.local @10.0.10.11
;; -> no SRV records (SERVFAIL)
```
that nameserver is CoreDNS in the same AZ.

marta: checking consul health: 
```
curl -s http://consul-us-east-1b.internal:8500/v1/status/leader
""  # empty -> no leader responding from this AZ endpoint
```
consul endpoints in us-east-1b are flapping replies. Other AZ endpoints (1a/1c) look healthy.

alex: quick impact summary for support: some internal control-plane RPCs failing, external API customer impact observed as elevated 5xx at the edge (not full outage, intermittent). Tagging support_lead.

support_lead: notified support channels, posting customers potentially affected list to status page. Draft message: "We are investigating increased internal service discovery errors in a subset of hosts in us-east-1b; some APIs may see transient 5xxs. No data loss reported."

samir: root cause hypothesis: partial network partition between compute nodes and service discovery backend in AZ us-east-1b — packets between CoreDNS pods and Consul/etcd members in the same AZ experiencing loss, causing SRV lookups to fail and Consul failing to answer leader queries. Need to verify overlay and node-level networking.

infra-bot: @alex performed automatic detection rule: core-dns-srv-health-drop > 30% for 3m, triggered runbook step: notify oncall.

alex: mitigation plan (short): 1) divert traffic off us-east-1b for latency-sensitive routes, 2) restart CoreDNS deployment in AZ us-east-1b to force re-register and reestablish connections, 3) if Consul leader not recover, redirect discovery queries to cross-AZ consul endpoints as a fallback.

marta: running leader check and trying soft restart of coredns in the AZ: 
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide | grep us-east-1b | grep coredns
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns --field-selector spec.nodeName=ip-of-node-in-us-east-1b
```
restarting one CoreDNS pod now (rolling, not all).

alex: while coredns rolling restart is happening, I'm updating routing policy for runtime -> prefer us-east-1a for new sessions: 
```json
{"route_policy": "prefer: us-east-1a", "scope": "control-plane"}
```
this is a short window mitigation — will monitor error rate.

june_ops: applying consul fallback: point local service discovery queries to cross-AZ consul proxies (consul-proxy.us-east-1a internal). Patch applied to runtime-agent config in us-east-1b nodes.

samir: good. after CoreDNS restart a few pods recovered, dig now returns SRV records again from restarted node: 
```
$ dig +short SRV _api._tcp.service.namespace.svc.cluster.local @10.0.10.11
0 10 8080 host-123.us-east-1a.internal.
0 10 8080 host-124.us-east-1a.internal.
```
error rate falling to ~8% in the AZ.

alex: moving to watch. Leaving incident channel open for 20m. Handing off to @samir for follow-up and post-incident. Notes: applied routing preference and coredns rolling restart, consul-proxy fallback in place.

samir: taking over. Action items for next hour: 1) run network path checks between nodes and consul in us-east-1b (tcptraceroute, mtr), 2) collect tcpdump on a couple CoreDNS pods to see where packets drop, 3) validate if cloud provider had an AZ fabric event (opening ticket).

support_lead: customer-facing status update posted: "Investigating higher than normal 5xx; mitigation underway — traffic rerouted off an impacted AZ; updates in 30 minutes."

alex: handing off full context: logs, commands run, config changes noted in thread. Marking myself reachable for 30m if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:

samir: received handoff. I'll escalate to network team if packet loss confirmed. Tentative severity: P1 -> will drop to P2 once error rate <5% and routing fallback removed.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — 19m since start. Status: partial mitigation in effect. Next update scheduled at +30m.

marta: capturing debug outputs to /var/tmp/incidents/1977778888-debug.tar.gz and will upload to the incident bucket for postmortem.

samir: last note — once we restore normal routing, we should run a canary traffic test to ensure SRV resolution remains stable before fully removing fallback. Scheduling that in 45m.

support_lead: thank you team. Updating customers with ETA +45m for full resolution.

alex: leaving channel now. Good work.

samir: closing active paging, keeping channel open until postmortem artifacts uploaded.
